description: Tree-parallel MCTS lets several threads grow one tree. Each thread, under the tree's lock, descends to a new leaf and marks its path as waiting, which other threads' selection counts as a loss (*virtual loss*), so they spread over different lines; outside the lock it values the leaf with its own evaluator and generator; under the lock again it backs the value up. The result is that of one search with more simulations, not a sum of trees as in root parallelism, and which thread reaches which leaf depends on scheduling, so a seed does not reproduce it. It pays off only when valuing a leaf costs far more than selecting it: with leaves of about a microsecond every added thread made it slower, as the threads queue for the lock, while with evaluations of about 30 microseconds eight threads beat root parallelism. Here it is `search_shared`, behind the `parallel` feature; use it with a costly evaluator such as a network, and root parallelism otherwise.

papers.authors: Guillaume M. J.-B. Chaslot, Mark H. M. Winands, H. Jaap van den Herik
papers.title: Parallel Monte-Carlo Tree Search
papers.venue: Computers and Games (CG 2008), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
